clue.text: Don't change this lad's headgear

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to leave a passage as it was
a son is a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to alter the hat a particular boy wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'lad' is a link meaning 'has', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat named after its American maker, so a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Sunny race in suburbs of Sydney

indicators.note: the race sits inside those outer letters
suburbs lie at the edges of a city, so only the outer letters of the city name are used

parts.note: the mile is a running race distance

explanation.surface: A cheerful running race held in Sydney's outer districts.
explanation.walkthrough: MILE goes between S and Y, the ends of Sydney.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley person is cheerful and good-humoured, like a sunny disposition.

clue.text: Finished importing uranium provided

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the U goes inside the word for finished

parts.note: ended means finished
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A trade deal over uranium imports has concluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Endued is an old word for endowed, supplied with a quality, so provided.

clue.text: Bardot, say, dodges unruly head of state after congress

indicators.note: the shuffled letters and the head letter come after the word for congress

parts.note: congress is an old term for sexual intercourse

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Brigitte Bardot sidesteps a wayward head of state after a political conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' suggests a parliament but is sexual congress. DODGES is shuffled to GODDES, then S ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French film actress Brigitte Bardot was a 1950s and 60s screen sex symbol, an example.

clue.text: Dark man on board heading off

indicators.note: the first letter, its head, is taken away

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A dark figure on a ship's deck turns away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark as a noun is the time after sunset, as in 'home before dark', the hours of night.

clue.text: Nancy's to dine, hosting a boss

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so the French verb holds the A within it

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, so its word for 'to dine' is the French verb manger

explanation.surface: Someone called Nancy is going to have dinner with a boss as her guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name but is the city in north-east France, signalling a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the person in charge of staff, the role of a manager.

clue.text: Atomic group's spy meets university lecturer in vehicle

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: the university and lecturer letters go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A secret agent meets an academic inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive, matching the adjective: of a molecule.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is a group of bonded atoms, so molecular means belonging to such a group.

clue.text: Book centre out for Christmas

indicators.note: the central letter of the five is removed

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: A shop sets out a book display in the middle for Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: NOVEL loses its middle letter V.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël is the French word for the festive season, used in English carols and cards.

clue.text: Frenchman and Yank upset one managing plots

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
to yank is to pull or drag

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and an American, both upset, are scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is the verb drag. RENE then DRAG, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots here are patches of land, and someone who tends them grows plants.

clue.text: They entertain camp old soldiers

definitions.meaning: the uniformed entertainers at British Butlins holiday camps wear red jackets
British infantry of past centuries wore scarlet tunics

explanation.surface: Veteran troops put on a show at their encampment.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlins is a chain of British holiday camps whose staff entertainers are known by their red jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: The name fits both holiday-camp entertainers and historic British army troops, both dressed in scarlet.

clue.text: It may consist of cards in packs, as stated

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: packs of cards are decks, so 'in packs' is 'in decks'

explanation.surface: A description of something made up of playing cards gathered in packs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In decks' said out loud matches the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A card index is a filing system built from many cards, one per entry.

clue.text: Plant study by staff after record's retrieved

indicators.note: the study and staff come after the turned record in the answer
read as re-trieved, brought back, so the word for record is turned round

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
a den is a private room for working, a study
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A plant is studied with a stick once a record has been fetched back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrieved' looks like fetched back; split as re-trieved it signals the record turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall garden and wayside plant with yellow flower spikes.

clue.text: Big wheel in London to call meeting of viewers

parts.note: the London Eye is the giant observation wheel on the South Bank of the Thames
to contact someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A summons to gather tourists at the London Eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' are eyes: the definition is two people's gazes meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: When two people look straight into each other's eyes their organs of sight meet.

clue.text: Personnel screen English Oscar star

indicators.note: to screen is to shield, so the personnel letters wrap round the English letter

parts.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A personnel department vets an English film star who has won an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' and 'Oscar' suggest cinema, but screen means enclose and Oscar is a radio code letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a story or film is its leading character, its protagonist.

clue.text: Peter puts up 20 homes for agents

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to house someone is to put them up

explanation.surface: A man called Peter gives accommodation to secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the answer to 20 down, so the definition reads 'secret homes for agents'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies and protected witnesses are hidden in secure dwellings kept by intelligence services.

clue.text: Bizarre legend about Philby, for one

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange and twisted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A strange story is told about the notorious British spy Kim Philby.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle LEGEND and ABOUT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim Philby worked for British intelligence while secretly spying for the Soviet Union, an example of a spy serving two sides.

clue.text: Don turned off, such are Wordsworth's ways

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An academic switched off when reading Wordsworth's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem begins 'She dwelt among the untrodden ways'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths no one has walked on are unvisited, the wild places of the Lucy poem.

clue.text: Traveller briefly repelled girl viewer

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the shortened word is reversed
briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Traveller is a name used for Roma and Irish travelling people
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A wandering man is rebuffed by a girl watching him.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten the word to GYPS, which turned back gives SPYG.
explanation.definitionFit: A small telescope is an instrument for looking at distant things, a viewer.

clue.text: Collateral damage done to city user

indicators.note: damaging the words breaks them up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Collateral damage is inflicted on a person using the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collateral damage' reads as one phrase, but collateral is the definition and damage the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged against a loan, a guarantee of repayment.

clue.text: Journalist stayed in Parisian stone flats

indicators.note: the editor and the sitting go inside the French stone

parts.note: pierre is French for stone, as a Parisian would say it
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
sat as in stayed put, remained seated

explanation.surface: A reporter lodged in stone-built apartments in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The French stone is split after its second letter to take the journalist and the sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small flat kept for occasional stays in a city; the plural matches 'flats'.

clue.text: A bundle of surprising letters left on shelf

indicators.note: a bundle is a bunch taken together, so a run of consecutive letters is taken

explanation.surface: A pile of unexpected letters has been left lying on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left on shelf' looks like where the letters lie; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left on the shelf has never married, so remains unmarried.

clue.text: Small island, close to front, private

indicators.note: the close, the final letter, moves to the front of the word

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A small island near the front line is kept private.
explanation.walkthrough: CRETE's last letter E moves to its start, giving ECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secret is kept hidden, known only to a few, so private.

clue.text: Grand Polish food

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to rub something is to polish it

explanation.surface: A description of a fine dish from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for something to eat, any meal or provisions.

clue.text: Undermine company male with potential

parts.note: someone with promise shows potential

explanation.surface: A firm's promising man is set to sabotage things.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise a plan or position is to weaken or endanger it, to undermine it.

clue.text: Quizzes police sergeant about Unionist politician

indicators.note: about means around, so the sergeant's letters go round the others

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A police sergeant questions a Unionist politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information.

clue.text: Plucky people may have to pluck this

definitions.text: people may have to pluck this
definitions.meaning: shot birds such as pheasants must have their feathers plucked before cooking

explanation.surface: Brave people may need to gather up courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both spirited and ready, and wild birds hunted for food.

clue.text: Scottish case review, one specifically with limits in UK

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
viz, short for videlicet, means namely or specifically
and means together with

indicators.note: only the outer limits of the full name are kept, its middle stripped away

parts.note: UK stands for United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A Scottish legal review is described as being, namely, confined within British borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out UK in full and keep only its first and last letters, U and M. The answer is a Scots law term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law, avizandum is a judge's taking a case away for private consideration before giving judgment.

clue.text: Portion of asparagus revolts pet

indicators.note: to revolt is to turn over, so the run is read backwards
a portion is a part, so a run of the vegetable's letters is taken

explanation.surface: A piece of asparagus disgusts a pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolts' looks like disgust but means turn: RAGUS from asparagus read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is an endearment, like darling or sweetheart, a term for one's pet.

clue.text: Very little money inspires Yankee oil producer

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer pieces take the letter inside

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
a bean is a tiny sum, as in not having a bean
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tiny sum of cash motivates an American to produce oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspires' looks like motivates but means breathes in, so the Yankee letter goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya plant's beans are pressed for a widely used vegetable cooking oil.

clue.text: Questionable cult defends American power

indicators.note: the sect stands guard round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a sect is a religious group, a cult
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A dubious cult protects American power.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is open to doubt, dubious, so it is questionable.
